title: Special Marine Warning
location: Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20 NM; Waters from South Santee River SC to Edisto Beach SC extending from 20 to 60 NM

details.description:
For the following areas...
Waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach out 60 NM...

At 237 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts
was located 9 NM southeast of Charleston Sixty, moving southeast at
15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Doug Mellichamp Reef, Comanche Reef, Capers Mid Shelf, Y-73 Reef
and Edisto Buoy.
details.instruction:
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with this storm.

Frequent lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

title: Beach Hazards Statement
location: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

details.description:
* WHAT...Increased threat of sneaker waves expected.

* WHERE...The Lost Coast and the Mendocino Coast.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.
details.instruction:
Don't be fooled by an ocean that looks calm.  There can be
30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

title: Flood Advisory
location: Miami-Dade, FL

details.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
county, Miami-Dade.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 229 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Miami, Miami Beach, Coral Gables, Key Biscayne, Surfside,
Virginia Key, North Miami, Miami Shores, North Bay Village,
Port Of Miami, Fisher Island, Downtown Miami, Marlins Park,
Coconut Grove, Bay Harbor Islands and Bal Harbour.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Charleston, SC

details.description:
At 228 PM EDT, local law enforcement reported flash flooding in Mount
Pleasant and Isle of Palms where a number of roads are closed. Cars
were also reported submerged in spots. As much as 3 to 5 inches of
rain have fallen across parts of Mount Pleasant, Isle of Palms and
surrounding areas since just before 1 PM. While rainfall rates are
lowering, moderate to locally heavy rainfall will persist and the
risk for additional flash flooding continues.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Pleasant, Isle Of Palms, Sullivan's Island, Mount Pleasant
Towne Centre, Boone Hall Plantation, Sullivans Island, Seaside
Farms, East Cooper Regional Medical Center and Snowden.
details.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

details.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures 110 to
115 and lows in the mid 80s to low 90s.


* WHERE...Coachella Valley, San Diego County Deserts, and San
Gorgonio Pass near Banning.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Major to locally Extreme HeatRisk. Elevated
low temperatures will limit overnight relief from the heat.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

title: Marine Weather Statement
location: Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20 NM

details.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...

At 204 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. These thunderstorms were
located along a line extending from Palm Beach Shores to near Palm
Beach, moving southeast at 5 knots.
details.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

Waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on the alert in
case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

title: Special Marine Warning
location: Biscayne Bay; Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM; Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas

details.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 245 PM EDT.

* At 202 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from Sunny Isles to
near Cape Florida, moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Lauderdale-By-The-Sea, Key Biscayne, Hallandale, Biscayne Bay,
Black Point, Bay Harbor Islands, Port Everglades, Elliott Key,
Golden Beach, Triumph Reef, Surfside, Coral Gables, Indian Creek,
Sunny Isles, Convoy Point, Turkey Point, Fort Lauderdale, Pacific
Reef, Cape Florida, and Virginia Key.
details.instruction:
Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Frequent lightning is occurring with these storms. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
